name: Sum of divisors
formula: n = p_1^{a_1} \cdots p_k^{a_k} \implies \sigma(n) = \prod_{i=1}^{k} \left(1 + p_i + p_i^2 + \cdots + p_i^{a_i}\right)
whenToUse: A question asks for the sum of all divisors of a number, or the sum of only its odd or only its even divisors.
pitfall: Each bracket starts at $1$ (the power $p^0$). For odd divisors only, drop the factor of $2$ entirely; do not just remove the $1$ from the bracket.
derivation: Expanding the product gives every term $p_1^{e_1} \cdots p_k^{e_k}$ with $0 \le e_i \le a_i$ exactly once, and those are exactly the divisors of $n$.
